conclusion: This Native-only run reaches only head 2739, below the reported 3381 rollback window. A memory-mode WAIT_REG_MEM command read 0x1 at 0x1B964004 while requiring equality to zero and remained false through poll 7000. The ring later resumed at the capture-deadline shutdown and emitted head 2737 then 2739; no ordinary guest writer or wait completion record was captured. This localizes a long synchronization stall but does not explain the earlier 3381->3375 write or prove the memory transition that released this wait.

interrupt_dispatch_join.interpretation: This is a timestamp/order join to a unique continuous PM4 interrupt window. Process 1 records callbacks observed inside the guest wrapper; Process 2 records the outer guest callback and data passed to ExecuteInterrupt. This does not prove callback payload or guest semantic equivalence.
interrupt_dispatch_join.join_method: exact gpu_dispatch_id; one P2 interrupt may own multiple nested P1 callbacks

wait_reg_mem_observation.interpretation: The ring later resumed and wrote events 2740-2743, so it left this wait before processing them. That burst occurred at the capture deadline and within 0.473 s of the title termination log. Because the wait completion log was suppressed by the existing first-16-waits cap and no memory transition/writer was captured, this does not prove a guest-side release during ordinary gameplay; treat the burst as shutdown-tail evidence.
wait_reg_mem_observation.post_wait_progress: The ring later emitted EVENT_WRITE_SHD head 2737 then 2739 from subsequent batches before title termination. The exact time/value transition that released this wait is not logged.
